rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty-one builder trees go (a row of torrey pines, corals and queen palms every 6 m along the back fences, fan palms 3-3.4 m from the houses, a few on the lawn); six come back on their own spots, about one for every two or three houses: by the picnic table, on the open lot corner, one back yard, and two on the old back fence row 51 m apart.

trees.why: the shared back lawn with the picnic table and the shade sail: a magnolia beside them
the same lawn 23 m east, 13 m from any wall: the lawn's second tree
the big open lot corner, 35 m from the walls: one norfolk pine, a landmark seen from the street
the south-west back yard, 6.7 m from the house: the yard's tree
the west end of the north back fence row: one of its two trees kept (it had one every 6 m)
the same row 51 m east: its second tree
